Details surrounding the incident remain limited at this time. The Escambia County Sheriff's Office has not yet released an official statement with additional information about…
item.content:encoded:
Bradley Vinson, son of newly elected Escambia County Commissioner Joe Vinson, died Sunday after being struck by a bullet on the Blackwater River, according to Miramar News.

Details surrounding the incident remain limited at this time. The Escambia County Sheriff's Office has not yet released an official statement with additional information about the circumstances of the death.

Vinson was recently elected to the Escambia County Commission and was preparing to take office. The family's loss comes as Vinson prepares to begin his tenure representing the county.

The City of Spanish Fort is offering residents a convenient way to tackle pre-holiday cleanup during the Thanksgiving season. According to the city's announcement, Spanish Fort has set up dumpsters available through Monday as part of a "Tidy the City" event designed to help residents dispose of yard waste, old furniture, and other items ahead of the holiday week.

The move comes as many households in the area prepare their properties for family gatherings and holiday entertaining. Free dumpster access removes a potential barrier for residents who might otherwise delay cleanup projects or have difficulty arranging private disposal options.

City officials have not announced specific dumpster locations or hours, so residents should check the City of Spanish Fort's official social media channels or contact city hall for details on where to drop off materials.

item.title: Free pet adoptions come to Escambia County Dec. 1-11
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Escambia County Department of Animal Welfare is partnering with the BISSELL Pet Foundation to offer free adoptions for dogs and cats one year or older from Tuesday, Dec. 1 through Friday, Dec. 11. The "Empty the Shelters" event waives adoption fees for older pets, though a $15 licensing fee applies to Escambia County residents. Younger animals…
item.content:encoded:
The Escambia County Department of Animal Welfare is partnering with the BISSELL Pet Foundation to offer free adoptions for dogs and cats one year or older from Tuesday, Dec. 1 through Friday, Dec. 11. The "Empty the Shelters" event waives adoption fees for older pets, though a $15 licensing fee applies to Escambia County residents. Younger animals will still carry adoption fees of $50 for puppies and $25 for kittens.

All adoptable pets come spayed or neutered, vaccinated, and microchipped. The shelter encourages the community to visit and consider providing forever homes to the many animals currently available. A complete list of adoptable pets can be found at 24petconnect.com.

The Escambia County Animal Welfare and Adoption Center is located at 200 W. Fairfield Drive. Hours are Monday through Friday from noon to 5 p.m., and Saturday and Sunday from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. More information is available at MyEscambia.com/animal-welfare or by following the department on Facebook and Instagram @EscambiaCountyAnimalWelfare.

"Empty the Shelters" is the nation's largest funded adoption event, having helped more than 431,000 pets find homes since 2016 through partnerships with hundreds of animal welfare organizations across the U.S. and Canada.

item.content:encoded:
The City of Pensacola will host a groundbreaking ceremony at 8:30 a.m. Tuesday, December 1, beneath the I-110 overpass to mark the official start of construction on the Hollice T. Williams Park Stormwater Park project.

The 1.3-mile park project will transform the historic area under I-110 into a community space while honoring the history and legacy of neighborhoods that once stood in that location. According to a city announcement, the project represents what officials describe as an important investment in the community and an opportunity to recognize the people and history central to Pensacola.

The groundbreaking ceremony is open to the public. For more information, contact the City of Pensacola Public Information Office at 850-435-1629.

item.title: Milton Officials Planning Smaller Christmas Celebration Following Hurricane Isaias
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: MILTON, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Milton officials are working toward a smaller community Christmas celebration after Hurricane Isaias disrupted the city's traditional holiday plans. During Thursday's City Council work session, members expressed support for holding an event Saturday, December 12, at Jernigan's Landing. Councilman Robert Leek raised…
item.content:encoded:
MILTON, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Milton officials are working toward a smaller community Christmas celebration after Hurricane Isaias disrupted the city's traditional holiday plans.

During Thursday's City Council work session, members expressed support for holding an event Saturday, December 12, at Jernigan's Landing.

Councilman Robert Leek raised the possibility of bringing residents together for a holiday gathering despite the city's ongoing hurricane recovery.

City Manager Ed Spears said a smaller event could include a Christmas tree lighting, holiday music, hot chocolate and food trucks.

One possibility discussed was inviting the Milton High School chorus to perform Christmas carols.

Council members also expressed interest in having Santa Claus attend.

Spears said he could organize an event using his existing spending authority, with costs not exceeding $10,000.

However, officials agreed that a traditional parade along Stewart Street would not be practical, and fireworks are not included in the current plans.

Mayor Heather Lindsay emphasized the need to avoid additional overtime costs for public works and public safety personnel while hurricane recovery continues.

Council members also discussed encouraging downtown businesses to participate, potentially through a holiday shopping event designed to bring customers into local stores.

The council reached a consensus to pursue the December 12 celebration, although final details and activities have not yet been announced.

item.title: Escambia Records Death as Dangerous Vibrio Bacteria Cases Rise Across Florida
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Florida health officials are warning residents about the dangers of Vibrio vulnificus, a potentially deadly bacteria found naturally in coastal and brackish waters. The Florida Department of Health has reported seven deaths associated with the bacteria this year, including one in Escambia County. According to…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — Florida health officials are warning residents about the dangers of Vibrio vulnificus, a potentially deadly bacteria found naturally in coastal and brackish waters.

The Florida Department of Health has reported seven deaths associated with the bacteria this year, including one in Escambia County.

According to state data updated November 19, Escambia County has recorded one confirmed case and Santa Rosa County has reported three.

Statewide, health officials have documented 36 confirmed cases and seven deaths in 2026, surpassing last year's total of 33 cases.

Vibrio vulnificus is sometimes called flesh-eating bacteria because severe infections can cause rapid destruction of skin and underlying tissue.

The bacteria can enter the body when an open wound comes into contact with contaminated saltwater or brackish water. Infection can also occur from consuming raw or undercooked shellfish, particularly oysters.

Health officials say residents should avoid exposing cuts, scrapes and other wounds to coastal or floodwater. Anyone handling raw seafood should also take precautions.

People with weakened immune systems or liver disease face a greater risk of severe illness.

Symptoms of a wound infection can include pain, redness, swelling, fever and blistering. Severe infections can progress rapidly and become life-threatening.

Anyone developing symptoms after exposure should seek immediate medical attention.

More information is available through the Florida Department of Health.

item.title: Pensacola Nonprofit ReadyKids Awarded Up to $1.39 Million to Expand Children's Literacy Programs
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — A Pensacola nonprofit focused on early childhood literacy is celebrating a major funding award that could significantly expand its services across Escambia County. ReadyKids has received a Bright Beginnings grant from the Escambia Children's Trust providing up to $463,000 annually over three years. The potential…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. (NewsRadio 92.3) — A Pensacola nonprofit focused on early childhood literacy is celebrating a major funding award that could significantly expand its services across Escambia County.

ReadyKids has received a Bright Beginnings grant from the Escambia Children's Trust providing up to $463,000 annually over three years.

The potential $1.39 million investment will support the organization's ReadingPals program, which connects children with volunteer mentors for one-on-one reading assistance.

ReadyKids plans to strengthen its prekindergarten services and expand into additional schools.

The organization is also continuing its expansion into kindergarten through support from United Way's Healthy Schools Escambia initiative.

Executive Director Kristy Craig called the funding a defining moment for the nonprofit, saying it will allow the organization to reach more children and strengthen partnerships with local schools.

The announcement comes alongside additional recognition for ReadyKids, which was recently named Nonprofit of the Year at the 2026 EntreCon awards.

The organization also received a $3,000 grant from MenPact of Pensacola to support volunteer mentoring relationships.

Founded in 2007, ReadyKids works with schools, families and community volunteers to improve children's reading skills and school readiness.

Residents interested in volunteering as ReadingPals can learn more at ReadyKidsFL.org.

item.title: Santa Rosa County hosting free tire drop-off day Dec. 5
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County residents can dispose of old tires free of charge this Saturday, December 5, at the Central Landfill in Milton as part of a Waste Tire Amnesty Day program run in partnership with the Florida Department of Environmental Protection. The event runs from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. at the landfill, located at 6337 Da Lisa Road. County officials…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County residents can dispose of old tires free of charge this Saturday, December 5, at the Central Landfill in Milton as part of a Waste Tire Amnesty Day program run in partnership with the Florida Department of Environmental Protection.

The event runs from 7 a.m. to 5 p.m. at the landfill, located at 6337 Da Lisa Road. County officials say each resident may drop off up to 24 tires, though large, heavy-duty, and racing tires are not accepted. Commercial tires from shops and vendors also won't be taken. You'll need to bring a valid photo ID showing Santa Rosa County residency to participate.

To speed up the process, the county is asking residents to pre-register online before Saturday using a QR code or by visiting SantaRosa.fl.gov/Tires. If you don't complete the registration form ahead of time, one will be available at the event. County officials say the new DEP requirements mean each tire disposed of must be logged and tracked.

For questions, contact the Santa Rosa County Environmental Department at 850-981-7135.
